provenance.notes: Format-0 position ids (a one-element base offset) with num_heads omitted, so head_size is 2 * cos_cache width and the head count is inferred from hidden_size.
The float16 arm of the same upstream case; ORT runs every RunTests case at float32 and float16 against the same expected values with a 0.002 absolute tolerance.
Format-1 position ids over three heads of six, with num_heads omitted so the head size comes from the cache width.
The float16 arm of the same upstream case.
Two batches of eight tokens over four heads of six, gathered through a format-0 base offset of zero.
The split-halves pairing over the same two-batch geometry and a format-0 base offset.
Partial rotation: four of six head elements rotate and the two-element tail is copied unchanged.
Packed batching: the sequence is longer than the cache, which upstream permits only under is_packed_batching=1. Every gathered row still indexes the cache.
Rank-4 BNSH input with a rank-2 cache and a format-1 position table. The opset-23 file is the only upstream source of numerically checked rank-4 rotary data; the two ops share this math exactly.
Rank-4 BNSH input over two batches, four heads and eight tokens, with num_heads left unset because a rank-4 head count comes from the shape.
Four-pair route at the Llama head size over two batches whose position rows differ, so a batch or token index mistake changes the values.
Float16 rotary embedding with the same rank-three table geometry as the corresponding float32 case.
Interleaved pairing on the four-pair route: head size 16 is exactly two rotation groups per head, so the deinterleave and reinterleave both run.
Format-0 base offset of three: the four tokens read cache rows 3 through 6, which a token index mistake would move.
A rank-0 scalar position id, the other spelling upstream accepts for a base offset.
Interleaved float16 with a base offset, the decode-loop spelling.
Partial rotation at the Phi-2 geometry: 32 of 80 elements rotate and the 48-element tail is copied by the remaining rotation groups.
A short rotary window inside a wide head, so most of the four-pair route's groups take the tail copy.
Enough rotation groups per slice that the workgroups tile the slice several times over, exercising the strided per-lane item loop rather than its guard.
Rotary dimension eight and the paired rotary-dimension-four case check small rotary windows at the same head width.
Rank-4 BNSH with two batches and three heads, so the pinned dispatch slice is a (batch, head) pair and every head of a batch must read the same position row.
Interleaved float16 rank-4 with non-monotonic positions.
Rank-4 with a format-0 base offset: the token index inside the slice is the row index directly.
The Phi-3-mini head size of 96 with a 48-element rotary window, which clears the four-pair route's rotary gate and leaves a 48-element tail.
Two batches sharing one base offset, so a slice-to-batch mistake shows up as a wrong head row rather than a wrong cache row.
Head size 12 is not a multiple of eight, so the single-pair route carries it; two batches with different position rows.
A rotary dimension of four fails the four-pair route's rotary gate even though the head size clears it, so this is the high side of that boundary.
An odd head size with an even rotary dimension, which the contrib CPU kernel supports: the last tail group copies a single element.
Interleaved float16 on the single-pair route with a base offset.
Rank-4 head size 10 on the single-pair route with a zero base offset.
An odd rank-4 head size with a four-element rotary window; num_heads is set because upstream requires it whenever rotary_embedding_dim is, and is otherwise ignored at rank 4.
Five heads of six with num_heads omitted, so the head count is inferred as hidden_size divided by twice the cache width.
Single-token decode with a one-element position vector, the shape a decode loop emits.
The same single token spelled as a 1x1 position table. Upstream reads a rank-2 tensor as the table format however few elements it holds, so this is the other side of the format boundary.
The grouped-query key projection of the same decode step: eight heads instead of thirty-two.
